title: A component is just a function 🧩

slides.text: A component is just a function 🧩
slides.say: Here's the secret of React: a component is just a JavaScript function that returns UI.

slides.text: Export it, define a function, return markup.
slides.say: Three steps. Export the component, define a function with a capital name, and return some markup.

slides.text: The markup is JSX: it looks like HTML, but it is JavaScript under the hood.
slides.say: That markup is called JSX. It looks like HTML, but it is actually JavaScript under the hood.

slides.text: Markup on several lines? Wrap it in ( ).
slides.say: If your markup doesn't start on the same line as return, wrap it in parentheses. Without them, the lines after return are ignored.

slides.text: Components = reusable UI building blocks you can nest like HTML tags.
slides.say: Takeaway: components are reusable building blocks. Write them once, then use them like your own HTML tags.
